verdicts.quote: The default schedule has three steps, at 1, 7 and 14 days after the due date ... No reminder is sent before the first step date
A fully paid invoice gets no reminder ... A void or cancelled invoice gets no reminder ... negative because of a credit, gets no message ... marks one invoice "no reminders"
verdicts.missing: What happens to an invoice on a payment plan; disputes are only handled by a manual mark, not as a stop condition the system recognises.

verdicts.quote: An invoice of 1,000.00 USD with 400.00 USD paid, once overdue, gets reminders showing 600.00 USD and not 1,000.00 USD.
However often the system runs in a day, however often it restarts, the customer gets one message for each step of an invoice and never two for the same step.
A fully paid invoice gets no reminder from the moment the payment is recorded ... If payment is recorded at 08:59 and the send time is 09:00, no reminder for that invoice arrives
A failed delivery is tried again, for 3 attempts in all, at least 1 hour apart, within the step date
verdicts.missing: Escalation to a person when sending keeps failing; failures are only recorded in the history, with no alert.

verdicts.quote: With 10,000 eligible invoices on one step date, by the end of that date the history has exactly one entry with an outcome for each
verdicts.missing: The mail provider's rate limit and how the batch is paced to stay within it.

verdicts.quote: each overdue unpaid invoice that has a step date already behind it gets exactly one reminder at the first send time
Step dates and the send time are counted in a configured time zone, UTC by default
verdicts.missing: Whether the customer's local time is used, and whether weekends and holidays are avoided.

verdicts.quote: contains the text INV-1042, 600.00, USD and 2026-03-01 (or the same date in another clear form)
verdicts.missing: How the amount and currency are formatted for the recipient's locale.

verdicts.quote: The reminder history for the invoice shows a skipped entry for that step with a reason that the address is missing or invalid.
verdicts.missing: What happens when a message bounces after the mail service has accepted it.

verdicts.quote: The recipient is the invoice's customer contact address.
verdicts.missing: Which contact or contacts receive the reminder when the customer has more than one billing contact.

verdicts.quote: For each reminder handled, the history shows the time, the address used, the step and the outcome (sent, failed or skipped)
A reminder shows the invoice number, the outstanding amount with its currency, and the due date ... For an invoice with a payment link the message contains that link.
verdicts.missing: Whether the payment link expires, and what to do if it has.

verdicts.quote: The owner can set the schedule
verdicts.missing: Access control: who else, if anyone, may configure the schedule or stop reminders, and who may send a reminder by hand.

verdicts.quote: Turning reminders off stops all sending from that moment ... The owner can mark one invoice "no reminders"
verdicts.missing: Turning reminders off per customer, previewing or dry-running, and resending by hand.

verdicts.quote: the outcome (sent, failed or skipped), and for a failure or skip the reason
verdicts.missing: A view of what the system will send next.

verdicts.quote: a reminder due that day is delivered to the mail service by 10:00 that day ... The customer gets nothing for that step on a later day.
Reminders never change an invoice's data ... creating and editing invoices and recording payments all work and give the same results as they would with the service up.
